summary: Most visitors need a Liberian visa arranged before travel — through an embassy or Liberia's online eVisa channel — while ECOWAS citizens enter visa-free under the bloc's free-movement protocol, as do citizens of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, which left the bloc in January 2025 but remain on Liberia's exemption list.

Money order only, non-refundable; rush service adds USD 50–75. Other missions set their own fees.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says Liberia remains a predominantly cash-based society and that credit and debit cards are not generally accepted, except at a few major hotels and some larger supermarkets. A few ATMs in Monrovia accept Visa cards, but they often run out of money; it advises bringing enough US dollars to cover all expenses.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says Liberia is generally stable politically but the crime rate is high, mostly opportunistic theft; foreigners have been mugged in Monrovia's Mamba Point and Sinkor areas. It advises not carrying valuables in public, not walking around Monrovia or isolated areas after dark, and arranging transport in advance. There is no reliable ambulance service.

tips.text: Bring US dollars in cash. The UK Foreign Office advises bringing enough to cover all expenses: Liberia is predominantly cash-based, cards are not generally accepted, and banks can run short of both US and Liberian dollars.
Canada and the UK both say the rainy season runs from May to November, when many roads become impassable — plan up-country travel for the dry months.
Australia's Smartraveller says power and water outages are common in Liberia, there is no landline telephone service and mobile phone communication may be disrupted — plan accordingly.
Get your yellow fever vaccination before applying: the visa application needs a copy of the record, and you should carry the yellow card with your passport.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Liberia?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. Visas are issued in advance by Liberian embassies, and an online eVisa channel has been introduced. Confirm the current online option with the nearest mission. ECOWAS citizens enter visa-free under the bloc's free-movement protocol; the Liberian consulate's exemption list still includes Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, which left ECOWAS in January 2025.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Liberia?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders must obtain a visa before travel from a Liberian embassy or consulate. The Consulate General in New York charges US citizens USD 180 for a three-year multiple-entry visa. Liberia's online e-visa, issued at Roberts International Airport, is for applicants with no Liberian embassy in their country.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Liberia?
faq.answer: Only with approval in advance. Liberia Immigration Service's online e-visa (USD 102.50, non-refundable) is approved before travel and the visa is then issued at Roberts International Airport only; apply at least 7 days before your flight. If there is a Liberian embassy in your country, you must apply there instead.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Liberia?
faq.answer: Yes. Liberia's consulate in New York requires a copy of your yellow fever vaccination record with every visa application, and the UK's travel advice says the same. Carry the yellow card with your passport.

faq.question: What currency should I bring to Liberia?
faq.answer: US dollars in cash. The UK Foreign Office says Liberia remains predominantly cash-based, cards are not generally accepted except at a few major hotels and some larger supermarkets, and ATMs often run out of money; it advises bringing enough US dollars to cover all expenses.
